chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl, from Abū Ismā‘īl al-Sarrāj, from Yaḥyā ibn Ma‘mar al-‘Aṭṭār al-Qaṭṭān, from Abū Basīr, from Abū Ja‘far (peace be upon him) who said:
Four thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, cry over him until the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: How many angels cry for Imam Husayn until the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* specifies that four thousand angels, described as 'shaggy and dusty' (signifying their humility and continuous worship), weep for Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) until the Day of Resurrection. This detail underscores the cosmic scale of the Karbala tragedy, illustrating that the martyrdom of the Ahl al-Bayt is not merely a historical event but an eternal reality witnessed by the celestial realm, reinforcing the Shia concept of the interconnection between the spiritual and physical worlds.
